sentence: The accept score ranks a draft by its deterministic findings first, then its confirmed major findings, then its minor findings, and any two different scores compare one way.

questions.ask: What should happen if an edit removes one deterministic finding and adds ten minor findings?
questions.code_today: The edit scores better, (0,0,10) < (1,0,0), so StrictImprovement keeps it.

questions.ask: What should happen if an edit turns one confirmed major finding into two minor findings with new keys?
questions.code_today: Kept: confirmed count drops; new minor keys are not checked.

sentence: StrictImprovement keeps an edit only when its score is strictly lower and it adds no new deterministic key and no new confirmed S5 or S4 key.

questions.ask: What should happen if an edit raises a confirmed S3 finding to S4 under the same key?
questions.code_today: Rejected: the key is new to the severe set.

questions.ask: What should happen if an edit adds an S5 finding that a model judge has not confirmed yet (not blocking)?
questions.code_today: It counts only as one more minor finding; the edit can still be kept.

questions.ask: What should happen if an edit fixes one deterministic finding but adds a different deterministic key (same count)?

sentence: StrictImprovement never keeps an edit whose findings are the same as before.

questions.ask: What should happen if the editor changes files but reflection reports exactly the same findings?
questions.code_today: Not kept (a tie), the files are reverted, and the rounds go on (only an unchanged, finished round stops them).

sentence: When rejects_early is true, keep reverts the edit whatever the reflectors add.

questions.ask: What should happen if a reflector should be able to clear a code-check finding?
questions.code_today: It cannot: reflection always starts from the code checks and only appends, which the soundness proof needs.

sentence: When the edit rounds end and the last kept draft has a blocking finding, LastClean restores the last kept draft that has none; when no kept draft is clean, the last kept draft stands.

questions.ask: What should happen if only the unedited projection is clean and every later round blocks: go back to the projection?
What should happen if a draft has no blocking finding but has a non-blocking floor finding?
questions.code_today: settle counts it as clean (it reads only blocking); the floor then judges it by floor and can block or fall back.
questions.looks: unclear: ask (can a code check emit floor=True, blocking=False?)

questions.ask: What should happen if settle gets no kept state?
questions.code_today: IndexError on states[-1]; the loop never passes an empty list.
